name: Racial nationalism
summary: Racial nationalism defines the nation by race and descent rather than by territory, culture or citizenship. It seeks a state or homeland for one race, restricts immigration and membership by race, and discourages mixing, and in its harshest forms has used eugenics, expulsion and conquest. Adherents treat group differences as largely innate and see diversity as a source of conflict; economic, religious and constitutional views vary widely.
scope: The genus as it exists in its most documented forms: the modern Western white nationalist current, represented by Jared Taylor's White Identity and American Renaissance, and the earlier Nazi racial state as the historical reference. Non-white variants (Black nationalism, Japanese minzoku or Korean minjok nationalism) are mentioned only in notes and are not modelled, and Taylor's book was read only in part. Economic, religious and procedural statements are mostly low-confidence inferences.

sources.title: Racial nationalism

sources.usedFor: Definition, racial purity, race-mixing bans, immigration and remigration, eugenics, ethnostate, Japanese and Korean variants.

sources.title: White Identity: Racial Consciousness in the 21st Century
sources.author: Jared Taylor (2011)
sources.usedFor: Diversity and conflict, ethnic kinship nations, racial preferences, welfare, group gaps, media and academic orthodoxy, white racial consciousness.

sources.title: Nazi Racism

sources.usedFor: Racial struggle, hierarchy, purity, Nuremberg laws, eugenics and Lebensraum in the Nazi form of racial nationalism.

sources.title: American Renaissance
sources.author: Southern Poverty Law Center
sources.usedFor: Homeland aims, race and IQ claims and Spencer's white-state proposal; a critical account.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Racial nationalists split: some would favour state care for the racial in-group, others reject the welfare state; the sources do not settle it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Economics is peripheral to the doctrine and adherents divide; nothing in the sources fixes a wage position.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Taylor treats economics as secondary to race and the movement spans free-market and economic-nationalist wings, so this is inferred as split.

public-ownership.rationale: Inferred: most racial nationalists prize private enterprise within the racial community, and Nazi policy left most industry privately owned under state direction.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No source ties the doctrine to a tax position; adherents are divided between populist and elitist currents.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred: independent unions sit uneasily with a race-first national community, and Nazi Germany dissolved free unions; modern nationalists are mixed.

property-fundamental.rationale: The doctrine subordinates property to racial interests but does not oppose it; adherents are split, so the answer is inferred as neutral.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Racial nationalists criticise elites and multinationals but offer no common regulatory program in the sources.

cut-welfare.rationale: Taylor links generous welfare to ethnic homogeneity and attacks immigrant welfare use, but wants it for the in-group rather than abolished, so adherents split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: collective worker ownership is a class doctrine at odds with the race-as-nation framing, which adherents treat as primary.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: security-state tolerance is typical of authoritarian racial regimes, though modern adherents fear being surveilled themselves.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The sources do not address drug policy and adherents are split between libertarian and moralist views.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Taylor says charges of racism are meant to silence debate; adherents see hate-speech law as aimed at them, though Nazi-style regimes censored their opponents.

strong-leader.rationale: Hashimoto's proposal and the Nazi leader principle show an authoritarian streak, but modern Western adherents are mixed.

state-harmful.rationale: Racial nationalism wants a state to embody and protect the race; Nazi doctrine made the racial state central.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: American adherents mostly favour gun rights as self-defence for the in-group; the sources are silent.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from the militarised racial state of Nazi doctrine and the movement's law-and-order framing of crime statistics.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred: racial nationalists tend to moralise about the family and national health; the sources do not discuss it.

decide-locally.rationale: Adherents want homogeneous local or ethnic units, but the national racial state is the core unit; sources do not resolve this.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred: Taylor stresses innate group differences in crime, which cuts against optimism about rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: Nazi ideology idealised the racially pure family as the nation's building block, and modern nationalists stress natalism and heritage.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred: Nazi policy persecuted homosexuals and traditionalist adherents oppose it, though some modern Western nationalists are indifferent.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred: racial nationalists are concerned with birth rates of the in-group; Nazi policy restricted abortion for Aryans.

more-religion-public.rationale: Strands diverge: some are Christian identitarians, others pagan or secular; the sources do not settle it.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Taylor says apologies for slavery and Jim Crow take neither honesty nor bravery and rejects white guilt and racial preferences as anti-white.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: biological determinism about race extends to a fixed view of sex in the Nazi tradition.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Taylor argues that racial preference is part of human nature and that the founding stock's identity should be preserved against dilution.

gradual-change.rationale: Inferred: the movement sees demographic change as urgent, and Nazi doctrine called for radical racial renewal.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Wikipedia reports that US white nationalists want immigration limited to people of European ancestry, some supporting remigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Race-first nationalism rejects supranational authority over the racial nation; Nazi doctrine treated it as hostile.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred: economic nationalism is common, though some adherents are free-market; economics is secondary.

nation-first.rationale: Nazi doctrine put the racial community above all others; Taylor presents ethnic loyalty as the basis of nations.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Taylor and similar writers oppose universalist moral claims that justify intervention; inferred from the in-group-first stance.

open-borders.rationale: Racial nationalism seeks to restrict immigration to preserve the nation's racial composition, which is incompatible with open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: The sources do not tie the doctrine to growth limits; adherents divide between pronatalist growth and eco-nationalism.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred: American adherents are generally sceptical of mainstream climate politics, but the sources are silent.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Taylor stresses innate human nature as limiting social engineering; otherwise the sources do not address technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is not a topic in Taylor, the Nazi sources or the Wikipedia overview, and adherents range from technophile to back-to-the-land, so I place them at neutral.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nazism came to power partly legally and partly through force; modern Western adherents mostly renounce violence, so they split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Taylor attacks elites and academics for orthodoxies, which suggests distrust of expert rule over popular majority interests.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred: Nazi economics kept private ownership under state direction rather than central planning; modern adherents mostly reject socialism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred: class-based ownership schemes are secondary to the race question, with modest rejection of socialist frames.

land-value-tax.rationale: A land-value tax is a Georgist reform that none of the racial nationalist sources discuss; nothing in race-based membership favours or opposes it, so neutral.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed by sources; heritage and family continuity cut against it, populism cuts for it.

basic-income.rationale: Taylor links welfare to diversity and criticises its cost; adherents generally oppose unconditional transfers, though in-group welfare is acceptable.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred: economic nationalism is common among racial nationalists, but sources do not settle it.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Nazi economic policy directed investment toward rearmament, but modern adherents are mixed.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Völkisch thought favoured the peasant smallholder, but sources do not make this a core claim.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The racial nation is a community of production and blood, and nothing in the doctrine supports abolishing wage labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Anti-banker themes appear in the Nazi tradition, but the question is not defining; adherents split.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Nazi Germany used state-run labour fronts, but modern adherents rarely discuss it.

one-party-rule.rationale: Hashimoto and Nazi Germany favoured one-party rule, but modern Western adherents usually contest elections, so it splits.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not a defining position; some adherents are monarchist, others republican.

democracy-best.rationale: Taylor warns demographic change endangers democracy and adherents see democracy as depending on a homogeneous nation, not as best in itself.

direct-votes.rationale: Taylor's concern is who makes up the electorate rather than how it votes, and Nazi and Hashimoto-style strands prefer leader rule, so adherents are split on direct legislation.

workers-councils.rationale: A class-based council system contradicts the primacy of race and nation.

right-to-secede.rationale: Spencer and Taylor seek a majority-white homeland, which implies secession rights, but this is inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Nazi doctrine held that racial hierarchy determined fitness to rule, and modern adherents accept innate group differences.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nazi doctrine embraced racial struggle and violence, but modern mainstream adherents disavow violence; inferred as mild disagreement.

war-builds-character.rationale: Racial struggle among peoples is central to Nazi thought, which glorified war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Some adherents are Christian identitarians, others pagan, secular or hostile to Christianity, and the race-defined nation does not itself settle church-state questions, so neutral.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Most racial nationalists ground law in nation or race rather than scripture, though Christian identitarians exist.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A race-based state exists to defend the racial community and would not privatise its defence.

military-superiority.rationale: Nazi doctrine saw military strength as essential to racial survival and expansion.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The core claim: Wikipedia defines it as national identity defined in racial terms, and white nationalists seek a white-only state or ethnostate.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nazi doctrine made race struggle, not class, the driver of history, according to the USHMM account.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Taylor argues group gaps are real and persist, so equal outcomes would be artificial; the doctrine denies innate group equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Racial nationalists favour racial homelands for their own group, which would imply sympathy in principle, but opposition to indigenous claims within the West is common.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Taylor rejects apologies and guilt over past wrongs; reparations are rejected as anti-white.

civilizational-union.rationale: White nationalists often call for pan-European or pan-white unity, supporting union by shared race rather than religion.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Taylor treats self-interest as natural, but racial nationalism subordinates the individual to the group.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The USHMM account of Nazi thought, which keeps the Aryan race pure and strong as the aim, places duty to the racial community above individual claims.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Völkisch strands romanticised nature, but the sources do not settle it.

limit-population.rationale: Racial nationalism is pronatalist for the in-group, though it supports limiting growth among others; mildly against.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Most adherents are not anti-industrial, but völkisch romantics were; inferred as mild disagreement.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The sources give no stance on technological disruption; modern adherents include both accelerationists and traditionalists, so neutral.

human-enhancement.rationale: Eugenic traditions favour enhancing the race, but modern adherents are divided.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from distrust of technocratic elites; not addressed in the sources.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between civil-libertarian and security views.

restore-past-order.rationale: Taylor describes the pre-1965 majority-white order as the founding nation and wants it back rather than progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Adherents treat race as the organising principle rather than pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Nazi movement used direct action; modern groups mostly use persuasion and elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Racial nationalist sources do not discuss prefigurative methods; the doctrine judges methods by their service to the race, so this is a weak, neutral inference.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The doctrine builds a modern racial state and has no primitivist strand.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The doctrine has no place for abolishing the division of labour; it is a Marxist utopian claim.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The racial nation rewards by hierarchy and not by need; Taylor says selfishness cannot be abolished.

production-for-use.rationale: Production for need rather than profit is a socialist formula that racial nationalist texts do not take up, though the movement's hostility to socialism makes slight disagreement likelier.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Nazi doctrine rejected Marxist class exploitation in favour of race as the fault line.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A class dictatorship contradicts racial nationalism, which makes the racial community the sovereign unit.

collective-farming.rationale: Völkisch thought valued the independent peasant farmer, and Nazi policy opposed Soviet collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Nazi doctrine attributed war to racial struggle rather than capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed; most adherents accept a taxing state for the racial nation.

harm-principle.rationale: Racial nationalists accept state restriction in the name of the nation's racial interest, not only harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The doctrine treats the racial group as the bearer of rights and interests, and Taylor defends white group interests.

conscription.rationale: Nazi Germany reintroduced conscription and the doctrine stresses duty to the racial nation.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The sources do not discuss exit versus voice; a doctrine built on belonging to a blood community stresses membership over leaving, so I infer mild disagreement.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is the vehicle of the people, not a business, in the Nazi tradition.

positive-liberty.rationale: The sources do not take up the positive-liberty debate, and the race-first state's concern is group survival rather than individual material means, so neutral.

media-academia-power.rationale: Taylor attacks media and academic orthodoxies and says charges of racism are meant to silence debate.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The SPLC records American Renaissance publishing and promoting race-and-IQ research, and the doctrine holds group differences to be innate.

organic-representation.rationale: Völkisch and Nazi thought spoke of organic community, but modern adherents are split.

total-state.rationale: Nazi doctrine claimed total control but modern adherents are mostly nationalist liberal-ish; split.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nazi doctrine called for racial renewal, and modern adherents speak of reviving a threatened people.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Nazi Lebensraum was expansionist, but modern white nationalists seek a homeland instead; split.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule by personal oaths between lords and followers is a feudal arrangement, not a racial nationalist one; the nation is defined by race and not by vassalage, so mild disagreement.

bound-labor.rationale: The Nazi regime used forced labour for racial reasons, but legally binding farmers to a lord is a feudal arrangement alien to the doctrine, so adherents reject it.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Taylor attacks claims that racial science is socially constructed and claims objective group differences exist.

universal-morality.rationale: Taylor rejects universalism that denies group loyalties, but does not deny universal moral truths outright.

single-common-good.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses a rationally determined common good; the Volk's interest is the nearest analogue, but adherents do not frame it this way, so neutral.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Spencer called his aim a sort of white Zionism, so some adherents back Israel as a model while antisemites oppose it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Race-based citizenship logic favours return rights for co-ethnics, though this is inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: The Wikipedia overview ties racial nationalism to blood rather than language, so language revival is not a defining concern; neutral.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Co-determination in firms is a socialist or social-democratic idea absent from the sources, and a race-first doctrine would treat it as peripheral or hostile, so mild disagreement.

school-vouchers.rationale: Taylor notes schools resegregate and whites flee; vouchers might help, but this is not addressed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not part of the race doctrine, and adherents are split between orthodox and nationalist-spending views, so neutral.

economic-freedom.rationale: Taylor treats economics as secondary and adherents range from free-market to economic nationalist, so I take no side.

rule-by-example.rationale: The Nazi regime as the USHMM describes it ruled by law-backed force and racial legislation, not by moral example, so mild disagreement is inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Taylor holds that peoples are extended families that should govern themselves, citing Connor's ethnonationalism.

force-without-un.rationale: Nazi policy ignored supranational constraints, but modern adherents are split on interventions.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Taylor appeals to empirical research and human nature but adherents also include religious identitarians and mystical völkisch strands, so neutral.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Taylor links welfare to homogeneity and criticises immigrant welfare use, so benefits should go to the in-group.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Taylor criticises welfare dependency and immigrant welfare use, so conditioning benefits on work fits his argument, though he does not state a rule; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Nazi Volksgemeinschaft stressed cooperation of classes within the race against internal class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Race-based nationalism prizes inherited culture and monuments of the race.

dominated-front.rationale: Racial nationalism is mostly a project of the majority in Western or East Asian states, and Wikipedia mentions anti-imperialist minjok nationalism only for Korea, so no common position.

workers-nation.rationale: The doctrine organises workers within the race-nation rather than as an international class, and the Nazi Volksgemeinschaft reflects this, so adherents agree.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Nazi ideology assigned distinct roles; modern adherents lean traditional.

ban-interest.rationale: Nazi propaganda attacked financial interest, but a ban on lending at interest is not a standard racial nationalist demand, so neutral.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Taylor describes private racial separation as natural but proposes no law; Nazi and apartheid regimes legislated it, so adherents split.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxist class-state view conflicts with the view of the state as embodying a people.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred: American adherents tend to side with right-populists on energy, but not addressed.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Racial nationalism denies that immigrants of other races can become part of the nation by assimilation; membership is racial.

elite-replacement.rationale: The Wikipedia white genocide conspiracy theory context shows the replacement claim is common, though Taylor avoids the word.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is not discussed in the sources, and adherents range from party-list to majoritarian views, so neutral.

national-mission.rationale: Racial nationalists focus on preserving their own people, not spreading government, though Nazi imperialism differed.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Taylor and the Nazi sources hold that sex roles reflect nature and not a system of male advantage, so adherents would deny the claim; inferred from the traditional-family position.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Taylor describes elites as imposing orthodoxies against the interest of the majority.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The Nazi regime forcibly sterilised people considered hereditarily unfit, and Wikipedia says the ideology often promotes eugenics.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred: nationalist and Nazi traditions resist accountability for state forces.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Not addressed; libertarian-leaning adherents say yes, statist ones say no.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Wikipedia says racial nationalism seeks racial purity, often by banning race mixing, as the Nuremberg laws did.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Nazi doctrine ranked races, and modern adherents like Taylor deny equal group capacity while some profess moral equality.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is an intra-Marxist dispute about revolution that racial nationalism does not engage; the Nazi doctrine rejected socialist internationalism, so mild disagreement.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Taylor describes the United States as founded as a self-consciously European nation and treats its settlement as legitimate rather than colonial wrongdoing, so adherents reject the label.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Different civil laws by religion is an Indian debate; racial nationalists want one law for the in-group and do not address religious personal law, so neutral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conversion law is a religious nationalist concern; a race-defined nation does not turn on religion, so adherents have no common view.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle protection is a Hindu nationalist demand and is not part of racial nationalism in any source I read; mild disagreement as an inference.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religious instruction in state schools is not a racial nationalist concern; Christian identitarians favour it and secular strands do not, so neutral.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Stalinist theory of the socialist state; racial nationalism does not address it, though it would endorse a strong state under threat, so neutral.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Taylor invokes democratic self-government, but authoritarian strands do not; split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export surpluses are economic nationalism that Taylor does not discuss and some adherents reject, so neutral.

population-transfer.rationale: Wikipedia reports remigration, mass deportation of non-white minorities, among supporters, and Spencer called for peaceful ethnic cleansing.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The USHMM account shows Nazi doctrine treating war and conquest for living space as legitimate, so adherents of that tradition reject an absolute ban on initiating force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The USHMM account shows Nazi thought saw history as a struggle among races in which the strongest dominate.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Racial nationalist parties are the ones such bans typically target, and Taylor complains that accusations of racism are used to silence debate, so adherents oppose them.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory is not discussed in the sources, and racial nationalists do not frame their politics in these terms, so neutral.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not addressed by Taylor or the Nazi sources; the Nazi state concentrated power, while American adherents revere the founders, so neutral.

vanguard-party.rationale: Not a Leninist doctrine, though the Nazi party claimed leadership; mildly against.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Priority to the poor of all groups clashes with the race-first priority and Taylor's claim that welfare should follow ethnic kinship, so mild disagreement.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Social housing sales are a British policy issue not covered in the sources, and nothing in the doctrine bears on it, so neutral.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Nazi Germany abolished free unions and strikes in the name of the national community, per general histories, but modern adherents do not focus on labour law, so mild agreement.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Taylor attributes group gaps to differences among groups rather than to population growth, and adherents do not give population as the main cause, so neutral.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Taylor writes in his introduction that diversity is not a source of strength but a source of conflict, which is the exact claim.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The doctrine favours rule by the racially or politically fit, not by lot.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian strand; the Nazi regime suspended protections after 1933.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price caps are not discussed in the sources and economic views among adherents vary, so neutral.

party-controls-media.rationale: Nazi regime controlled media, but modern adherents claim to defend free speech.

party-commands-army.rationale: Nazi forces swore personal oaths to the leader, but modern adherents do not discuss party control of the military, so neutral.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Restrictive citizenship follows from racial membership; the movement favours stricter rules.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay for legislators is not addressed by the sources and the doctrine has no stance on it, so neutral.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding party discipline is a Leninist norm; the Nazi party enforced it, but modern adherents work in loose movements, so neutral.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational pooling conflicts with racial national sovereignty, though pan-European racial unity is a minority view.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Nazi leader principle put military command in the leader, but modern adherents in parliamentary states do not take up the question, so neutral.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is a theological question that race-defined nationalism does not address, so neutral.

clerical-rule.rationale: In the USHMM account race, not clergy, is the ultimate source of authority, so senior religious scholars as rulers contradicts the doctrine.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Racial nationalists place loyalty to the racial nation above class solidarity, so they reject the Leninist idea that workers should wish their own government's defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Nazi regime censored degenerate art, but modern adherents oppose censorship of themselves.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential term limits are not discussed in the sources, and leader-centred strands favour unlimited tenure while American adherents revere constitutional limits, so neutral.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall elections are not addressed in the sources, and the doctrine has no stance on them, so neutral.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliances are not discussed by Taylor; some adherents want pan-white ties while others want strict nationalist isolation, so they split.

people-in-arms.rationale: A citizen militia in place of a professional army is not a stated racial nationalist aim; gun-rights sentiment among American adherents is not the same claim, so neutral.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The völkisch tradition behind racial nationalism, including Blood and Soil, idealised peasant life against the city, which I infer many adherents share.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-nationalism for co-ethnics, such as Pan-German unification, follows from defining the nation by race and ancestry rather than state borders; inferred.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Taylor attacks academic and media orthodoxies on race and diversity as detached from ordinary life, so adherents plausibly agree; inferred from that stance.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The USHMM account says Nazi thought ranked races, with Aryans as master race.

death-penalty.rationale: Racial nationalists are tough on crime, and Taylor points to group crime differences; the sources do not discuss capital punishment directly, so mild agreement is inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Traditionalist adherents oppose gender-equality curricula as part of their defence of the family, though the sources do not discuss it; mild disagreement.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Christian identitarians may favour it, but others rely on biological science for race claims, so adherents split on teaching creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Traditionalist and völkisch strands favour restriction while libertarian-leaning adherents resist, and the sources are silent, so neutral.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Nuremberg laws stripped Jews of citizenship and tied it to blood, per USHMM.

minority-language-support.rationale: A race-defined nation has no reason to fund minority languages, and Taylor opposes official multilingualism by implication, so mild disagreement is inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for religious minorities presuppose recognised minority groups, which the single-nation view disfavours, so mild disagreement; sources do not discuss.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Taylor and völkisch thought value conformity to heritage and group loyalty, so mild disagreement with Mill's praise of eccentricity is inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt relief for poor countries is not a concern in the sources; the in-group-first stance cuts against it, but other adherents resent banks, so neutral.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The question concerns anti-colonial movements, and racial nationalists do not address it; they care about race rather than property systems, so neutral.

constituent-assembly.rationale: A new constitution by elected assembly is not a stated racial nationalist demand, and adherents divide between constitutional restoration and authoritarian rewrites, so neutral.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The sources link authoritarianism to Hashimoto and Nazi strands but not to developmental rationale, so neutral.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Taylor argues group loyalty and in-group interest, not universal duties, and links poverty to group differences, so adherents reject a duty to give aid abroad; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The doctrine's emphasis on national sovereignty suggests nationalists would prefer an independent deterrent to dependence on an ally, but sources do not address it; low.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The doctrine does not fix a mode of choosing the head of state; Nazi doctrine used plebiscitary acclamation while modern adherents split.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Neither source treats monetary institutions; adherents split between anti-banker and orthodox views.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Spencer and Taylor seek a homeland where the group is a majority, which implies not trading away its territory; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Nazi doctrine subordinated property to the interest of the Volk, though modern adherents rarely discuss it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Whether the USSR was socialist is an internal Marxist dispute, and racial nationalists reject both views as Marxist, so neutral.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental precaution is not addressed in the sources, and adherents have no common position, so neutral.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred: allies of the same race would defend one another, but racial nationalists often distrust alliances; slight agree.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Nazi annexations were justified by racial claims, so adherents would not call them unlawful; modern adherents are split.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Nazi regime pressed churches into line, but Christian identitarians resist; split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Nazi leader merged state and party while modern adherents are indifferent to ceremonial heads of state, so neutral.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Adherents want racial homelands but also strong national unity; the sources do not resolve it.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A one-country-two-systems arrangement is a Chinese policy question that racial nationalism does not address, so neutral.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Nazi leader cult had quasi-religious features but did not claim divine descent, and modern adherents reject sacral rulers, so mild disagreement.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not part of the doctrine and adherents split between populist and market views, so neutral.

character-from-environment.rationale: The USHMM account says Nazis believed races have inherited traits that determine intelligence, creativity and strength.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Nazi leader principle placed the leader above law, but modern adherents invoke the rule of law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is not a stated goal in the sources, though some adherents favour grand racial destiny themes, so neutral.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The mixed constitution of classical political theory is not discussed in racial nationalist sources, so neutral.

leader-cult.rationale: Nazi Germany built a leader cult, but modern Western adherents are divided on it.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody rules are not covered by the sources, and traditionalist adherents favour mothers while men's rights sympathisers favour equal time, so neutral.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine about socialism that racial nationalism does not address; slight disagree from its anti-Marxism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred: property seizure is not part of racial nationalist programs.

refugee-return.rationale: Taylor links refugees and migrants to demographic change; return of refugees to homes elsewhere is not addressed, inferred as against.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Nazi regime claimed territory where Germans lived, and ethnic nationalists generally accept co-ethnic claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not part of the doctrine, which defines the nation by race rather than faith.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; some adherents criticise Islamic dress rules.

common-currency.rationale: A single currency across states erodes national sovereignty, so adherents committed to race-nation sovereignty would doubt it, but the sources are silent; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: White nationalism is a pan-ethnic movement uniting peoples of shared ancestry across borders, per Wikipedia's categorisation.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; minorities have no standing in a racially defined state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The question concerns Zionist debates; racial nationalists see minorities as belonging elsewhere.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nazi doctrine said race drives history, which opposes the Marxist materialist view.

ban-cartels.rationale: Anti-trust policy is absent from the sources and adherents are split on economic policy, so neutral.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed, and adherents include both anti-banker populists and pro-business conservatives, so neutral.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Taylor stresses majority self-interest and criticises elite orthodoxy; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for women in public bodies conflict with the traditional role views and hierarchical outlook of racial nationalism, so I infer disagreement.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Nazi autarky aims existed, but modern racial nationalists are split between protectionism and trade, so the closed bloc idea is not shared.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Social clauses in trade agreements are not addressed by the sources; adherents oppose such supranational standards but also oppose free trade, so neutral.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replacing material incentives with moral ones is a communist idea not found in the sources, so neutral.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foco theory is a Guevarist idea not found in the sources; mainstream racial nationalists disavow armed revolution, so neutral.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Racial nationalism upholds hereditary rank by race, but the sources do not address aristocratic titles, so neutral.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Taylor and similar writers want identity-affirming heritage teaching rather than apologetic curricula.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Nazi racial hierarchy ranked peoples but sought removal or domination rather than tutelage, and modern separatists reject ruling others, so adherents split.

patriotic-education.rationale: Taylor laments that whites are discouraged from racial pride and that history teaching is guilt-driven.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Taylor cites reverse-discrimination suits and criticises racial preferences as anti-white.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation by a public body is not discussed, and adherents split between anti-banker views and orthodoxy, so neutral.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Whether capitalism avoids collapse is a Marxist question that the sources do not take up, so neutral.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Nostalgia for former empire is not a defining claim; Nazi and Japanese examples sought expansion, but modern adherents focus on homeland, so neutral.

delink-world-market.rationale: Delinking is a dependency-theory strategy absent from the sources, and racial nationalists treat poverty as rooted in group differences, so neutral.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Leninist claim about workers in rich countries that racial nationalists do not discuss, so neutral.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Taylor notes that in private the races separate and criticises anti-discrimination law, framing separation as free association.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional limits are not addressed in the sources, and American adherents revere the founders while authoritarian strands do not, so neutral.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaty claims are not addressed in the sources, so neutral.

elective-rulers.rationale: Whether rulers are elected or hereditary is not settled by race-based nationalism, and adherents range from monarchist to democrat, so neutral.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: racial nationalists defend majority interests, not minority veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The right to resist a tyrant is a classical question the sources do not take up, so neutral.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary supremacy against the monarch is not a racial nationalist question, so neutral.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not part of the sources, though Nazi Germany passed animal protection laws, so neutral.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; Nazi Germany passed animal welfare laws, but not a core doctrine.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Duty of the privileged to those less fortunate is read by racial nationalists as obligation within the in-group, which I infer mildly supports the claim.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Racial nationalism is a mobilising politics that tells adherents to act for their people, so withdrawal contradicts it.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Taylor attacks media orthodoxy, but the specific claim is not addressed.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is a Marxist claim the sources do not take up; Taylor's attacks on elite orthodoxy are loosely similar, but it is not stated, so neutral.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency-theory claim contrary to racial-hierarchy explanations of poverty.

native-born-offices.rationale: Restricting offices to native-born citizens follows from racial nationalism's closed membership, and Wikipedia ties it to limiting the nation to one race; inferred as agree.

party-own-road.rationale: Independent roads to socialism are a communist issue that does not apply to racial nationalists, so neutral.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred: against foreign aid, with natural group differences; mildly agree.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Nazi revisionism demanded lost territory and ethnic nationalists commonly do.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Racial homeland logic favours it in principle, but adherents oppose it for Western settler states.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Racial nationalists regard anti-fascism as hostile to themselves, and Taylor complains about charges of racism being used to silence debate, so adherents reject it.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Adherents condemn communism but resist equating it with fascism, whose doctrine many of them partly inherit, so I infer mild disagreement.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Taylor disputes narratives of white guilt, though the sources do not discuss the Civil War cause.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Taylor rejects apologies for slavery and Jim Crow and defends heritage against shame narratives.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Traditionalist adherents tend to accept claims about male disadvantage, but the sources do not discuss it, so mild agreement is inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Sources do not discuss gendered violence; adherents range from traditionalist to men's rights views, so neutral.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Taylor argues societies differ by the people composing them, so institutions suit particular peoples.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political guardian role for the army fits authoritarian strands like Hashimoto's, but American adherents do not seek it, so neutral.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages for housework is a feminist demand absent from the sources, and traditionalist adherents prefer pronatalist family support, so neutral.

filial-duty.rationale: The Nazi and völkisch focus on the family as the root of the Volk suggests respect for parents, though not directly stated, so mild agreement is inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service exams are not discussed by the sources, so neutral.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalism is common among adherents and fits a race-first view of the nation's assets; I infer mild agreement without a source stating it.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Traditionalist family emphasis suggests adherents favour restricting easy divorce, though sources do not say so, so mild disagreement.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding delegates is a council-communist idea absent from the sources, so neutral.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not discussed in the sources, and adherents split between welfare-state and market views, so neutral.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Blood-and-soil thought tied people to land, but individual ownership persists; split.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control is not addressed by the sources and varies with the strand, so neutral.

single-official-language.rationale: Taylor presents English-only employment rules as defending Americans; inferred majority-language emphasis.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Blood-and-soil thought ties the land to the race, so barring foreign owners is a natural inference, but the sources do not state it; mild agreement.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Taylor says group gaps are real and persist across incomes and are not the result of bias, and cites reverse-discrimination suits.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Critique of consumer culture appears in both völkisch and left thought but is not a stated racial nationalist claim, so neutral.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert support for insurgents is not addressed in the sources, and adherents vary, so neutral.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Brezhnev-doctrine style of intervention in allied states is not addressed by racial nationalist sources, so neutral.

corporate-influence.rationale: Adherents attack elites but do not focus on corporate lobbying; Taylor targets media and academia rather than business, so neutral.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Nationalist distrust of foreign influence makes adherents likely to support limits on foreign-funded organisations, though not stated in the sources; mild agreement.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The Nazi regime promoted births among Aryans, and modern adherents emphasise birth rates of the in-group.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on home purchases by outsiders follow from the homeland and blood-and-soil emphasis, but the sources do not address it; mild agreement.

job-guarantee.rationale: A guaranteed job is not discussed in the sources, and adherents split on welfare-style economics, so neutral.

democratic-peace.rationale: The sources do not take up democratic peace theory, and the movement's scepticism of democracy promotion suggests mild disagreement.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: A philosophical-anarchist claim absent from the sources; the race-first state demands loyalty, so mild disagreement.

non-intervention.rationale: Strict non-intervention in other states is not a stated position; Nazi expansion violated it while modern adherents often favour staying out, so neutral.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union organisation form is not discussed by the sources, and the doctrine is wary of independent unions generally, so neutral.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The USHMM account describes Jews as a parasitic race and existential threat in Nazi doctrine; modern adherents vary.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The racially pure family is the Nazi building block and modern adherents defend marriage, so they would reject abolishing legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of information is not addressed in the sources, so neutral.

local-production.rationale: Blood and soil local production ideals versus modern economics; split.

informal-organisation.rationale: Small informal affinity groups are an anarchist model not found in the sources, and the movement uses formal organisations such as American Renaissance, so neutral.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Racial nationalists reject supranational and international legal constraints on the racial nation, and the Nazi regime ignored them, so adherents agree.

religious-nation.rationale: Wikipedia defines racial nationalism as defining the nation in racial terms, so adherents reject defining it by shared religion, though Christian identitarians partly overlap.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary deference is a Sinocentric concept; sovereignty-first racial nationalists reject submission to another state, so I infer disagreement.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regional revenue sharing is not addressed by the sources and adherents have no common position, so neutral.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Private personal belongings are uncontroversial and not discussed by the sources; the question concerns communal ownership of production, so neutral.

defeat-communism.rationale: Nazi doctrine was explicitly anti-Marxist, and modern adherents oppose communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service delivery mix is not discussed by the sources, so neutral.

religion-illusion.rationale: The sources do not take up the Marxist critique of religion; some adherents are pagan or atheist while others are Christian, so mild disagreement as an anti-Marxist inference.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Marxist claim of capitalism's progressive role is not discussed, and adherents are split on economics, so neutral.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Racial nationalists reject the premise that equality requires economic transformation, as they do not seek women's equality of that kind; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Public childcare conflicts with the family-centred view of the Nazi tradition, so I infer mild disagreement; the sources do not state it.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism existed in Nazi-era Germany, but it is not a general racial nationalist demand, so neutral.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with nations inside the state's borders are not addressed by the sources, so neutral.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small cooperative communes are a utopian socialist model alien to racial nationalism, so I infer mild disagreement.

majority-settlement.rationale: Nazi policy settled Germans in the East, and Hashimoto-era Japan did likewise; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Nazi doctrine claimed a third course between the two, but modern adherents split on economics, so they divide on the claim.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Spencer and Taylor stress attachment to homeland; ethnic nationalists generally treat historical tie as strong.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Some adherents deny it, others do not; the main strand avoids the topic.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Nazi regime persecuted homosexuals, but modern Western adherents range from indifferent to hostile, so they split.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Nazi doctrine supported it but modern adherents claim speech freedoms.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Blasphemy law is a religious state demand and race-defined nationalism does not make religious claims, so mild disagreement.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Wikipedia and USHMM do not say that colonies should serve the metropole, but Nazi Lebensraum policy exploited conquered peoples; modern adherents are split, so neutral.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: This is an Islamist doctrine with no counterpart in racial nationalism, which rejects it as foreign.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Takfiri removal of rulers is an Islamist idea outside racial nationalism, so adherents reject it.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct participation in workplace and community decisions is not stated in the sources, and the movement favours leaders and racial cohesion over deliberation, so mild disagreement.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Taylor rejects the premise that racial inequality results from oppression.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Traditionalist adherents oppose legal recognition of gender identity as part of their defence of nature-based roles; inferred, not stated in the sources.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is not discussed in the sources; Nazi euthanasia policy targeted the disabled, but modern adherents are split, so neutral.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Racial nationalists see themselves as beyond left and right in some strands, but sources do not state it, so neutral.

alienated-labor.rationale: The Marxist concept of alienation is not taken up by the sources, so neutral.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Concern with demographic change leads many adherents to see Muslim immigration as culturally alien, but Taylor's excerpted chapters do not state it; mild agreement.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Sources do not settle whether authority comes from God; Christian identitarians say yes, pagan and secular strands no, so neutral.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Restrictions on religious dress are not covered in the sources, and adherents are split, so neutral.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace harassment law is not discussed by the sources, so neutral.

social-market-economy.rationale: A social market economy is not addressed; adherents range across economic views, so neutral.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The USHMM account shows racial nationalism treating war and struggle between races as basic, and a race-state needs force, so adherents reject abolition.

rich-first.rationale: Unequal development as a stepping stone is a Chinese reform argument and not addressed here, so neutral.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Neutrality between great powers is not addressed by the sources, and adherents split between alignments, so neutral.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Succession of a leader by a child is not stated in the sources, and adherents range from monarchist to republican, so neutral.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit banks are a mutualist proposal not found in the sources, so neutral.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Resisting IMF terms is a development politics issue that sources do not address, so neutral.

property-franchise.rationale: Racial nationalism restricts membership by race, not by property, so the property-based franchise is not the nationalist demand, and I infer mild disagreement.

domination-women-nature.rationale: This ecofeminist claim contradicts the sources' naturalised sex roles, so adherents reject it.

reification.rationale: The Marxist concept of reification is not in the sources, so neutral.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Taylor complains of media orthodoxy but not that the rich own the press, so the claim is not stated; neutral.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule by published standing laws is a rule-of-law principle the sources do not discuss; the Nazi regime used decrees but modern adherents appeal to law, so neutral.

racial-franchise.rationale: Racial nationalism restricts national membership by race, and the Nuremberg laws stripped Jews of citizenship.

online-participation.rationale: Online deliberation is not addressed by the sources, so neutral.

open-government-data.rationale: Open records are not discussed by the sources, so neutral.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Interfaith marriage rules belong to religious nationalism; racial nationalists restrict by race and not by faith, so I infer neutral.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Nazi policy organised boycotts of Jewish shops starting in 1933, though modern mainstream adherents disavow boycotts of this kind, so mild agreement.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are a deliberative democracy idea that the sources do not address, so neutral.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Reinterpretation of religious law is a theological question outside racial nationalism, so neutral.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Concentration of wealth is not a racial nationalist concern in the sources, so neutral.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The Nazi regime persecuted homosexuals, and traditionalist adherents oppose open service, but sources do not say so; mild disagreement.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: State atheism is a communist policy; racial nationalists reject it, and Christian identitarians oppose it explicitly, so I infer mild disagreement.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Racial nationalists stress crime and order as Taylor does with group crime statistics, so they oppose abolition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Taylor argues diversity breeds conflict and favours separation over sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Sources do not address whether charity is better than the state for the poor, and adherents split between welfare-state and charity views, so neutral.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is a modern proposal absent from the sources, so neutral.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is not stressed in the sources, though adherents speak of racial extinction, so neutral.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Women's religious leadership is not discussed in the sources, and traditionalist adherents oppose it while others do not care, so neutral.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Marital authority is not addressed in the sources; traditionalist family views suggest paternal headship, but strands differ, so neutral.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Membership in the community is defined by race, so voting by foreign residents conflicts with it, and I infer adherents reject it.

rent-control.rationale: Rent caps are not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not a racial nationalist topic, so neutral.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Hitler Youth is the clearest historical example of drilled uniformed youth in racial nationalism, but modern Western adherents do not usually advocate it, so mild agreement.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is not addressed in the sources, so neutral.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign bases are not addressed by the sources, though sovereignty-minded nationalists tend to object; adherents are split, so neutral.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Official recognition of past genocides is a Holocaust-and-memory issue that some adherents reject, but the sources do not say, so mild disagreement is inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Rewarding labour over capital ownership is a producerist theme in völkisch thought, but not stated in the sources, so neutral.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Pacifism contradicts the racial-struggle view in the USHMM account of Nazi doctrine and the defence-of-race emphasis, so adherents reject it.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Racial nationalism defines the nation by common descent, which implies a continuous people from its ancient origins, so adherents agree; inferred from the blood-based definition.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The doctrine treats biological traits as fixed, as with race, so adherents reject social construction of sex; inferred from the Nazi biological determinism.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Fixed categories fit the biological determinism of the doctrine, so adherents reject dissolving the category of women; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Nazi movement built a martyr cult, and modern adherents honour figures who died for the cause, so I infer agreement.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Some strands see politics as a spiritual struggle between good and evil, others as racial biology, so neutral.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Taylor and Spencer want a homeland where their group is a majority, but not a spiritual centre for a diaspora, so neutral.

culture-before-state.rationale: The sources describe racial renewal as political, but the metapolitical strand holds that cultural change must come first, so adherents split.

god-not-male.rationale: Language for God is not discussed, and traditionalist Christian adherents object while pagans do not care, so neutral.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology is a view racial nationalists reject by default, though the sources do not address it; mild disagreement.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Nazi policy removed Jews from economic life and racial nationalists claim the economy should be in the hands of the national race, so adherents agree.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Pan-ethnic unity under one territorial unit follows from defining the nation by race, so adherents agree; inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Taylor argues that non-white groups already pursue explicitly racial interests and that whites should do the same, asking of such groups what is in it for them.

racial-pride.rationale: Taylor describes whites as discouraged from racial pride and calls for white racial consciousness, and he says apologies for past wrongs require neither honesty nor bravery.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred: independent unions sit uneasily with a race-first national community, and Nazi Germany dissolved free unions; modern nationalists are mixed.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; racial nationalists reject class as the basis of politics and the statement is a socialist debate.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents divide on economics and nothing in the sources fixes a position.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; constitutional design is not part of the doctrine.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: the racial state or racial community is the core unit, not the municipality, and Nazi Germany kept private ownership under state direction.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred: racial nationalism puts power in a national racial state, not in local assemblies bound by confederal limits.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; nothing in the sources bears on medical regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; nothing in the sources bears on science funding.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred: many modern adherents, deplatformed from banks and payment firms, favour financial privacy, but the sources record no position.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred: modern adherents face doxxing and deplatforming and commonly use pseudonyms, but the sources record no position.

person-over-state.rationale: Nazi doctrine subordinated the individual to the racial community, and Taylor makes group identity the basis of politics.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred: Nazi doctrine spoke of the soul of the race, but modern adherents are mixed between religious and secular views.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents want homogeneous units, but the sources do not settle how central or regional power is arranged.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; nothing in the sources bears on agriculture.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; blood-and-soil strands favoured the countryside, modern adherents are mixed; nothing is sourced.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Nazi doctrine sought conquest for racial living space, while modern white nationalists like Taylor favour non-intervention; adherents are split.

family-wage.rationale: The sources stress racial survival and family formation but state no wage policy; economics is peripheral and adherents divide.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The doctrine defines the nation by race and descent rather than by culture or language, so a shared language alone does not make a nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the aim of a single-race homeland with common membership, where separate religious electorates are not a feature.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from Taylor's view that elites and institutions push demographic change against the in-group's interest; the claim is of plots against the people more than literal partition.

free-public-college.rationale: Adherents divide on welfare-style spending, and the sources do not mention tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental policy is peripheral and adherents split between conservationist and market views; nothing in the sources fixes it.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the stress on handing the race's heritage and homeland to posterity; the sources do not frame it as a duty to future generations about the Earth.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Adherents stress innate sex and group differences and traditional roles, and the sources give no support for giving women's values extra weight in politics.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Nazi form built up arms and expansion, and the modern strand emphasises defending the in-group, so disarmament is unlikely; inferred rather than stated.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed; adherents who oppose elites might favour openness while state-minded ones accept secrecy, so they split.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from economic nationalism and the Nazi state's control over foreign exchange and trade; the modern strand mostly does not discuss it.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Adherents split between wanting the state to disarm other groups and valuing armed self-defence; the sources do not settle it.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Nazi state demanded military obedience and white nationalists value the in-group's martial defence; refusal is inferred to be rejected, though some oppose wars they see as fought for others.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Nazi state abolished independent unions in favour of the Labour Front, and the current gives economics little weight; inferred mild disagreement.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Economics is peripheral to the doctrine and adherents divide on welfare for the racial in-group.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are not discussed and adherents hold varied economic views.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Racial nationalists tend to prefer national autonomy and economic nationalism over redistribution to other countries; inferred from Taylor's focus on in-group interest.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Nazi movement took over and used the state rather than smashing it, and white nationalists seek a racial state; inferred disagreement.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The goal is a racially defined state; open pluralism in how a society is organised is inferred to matter less than racial unity, so only mild disagreement.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not discussed by the sources; adherents' views on environmental pricing vary.

sacred-nation.rationale: Racial nationalism treats the nation as a community of descent that persists across generations, as in the Nazi Volk, though 'sacred' is not always the term used.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student debt is not discussed and adherents divide.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The current sees the nation as a racial unit and tends to deny internal exploitation framings; inferred from its focus on race rather than regional class.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Taylor argues that races differ in innate traits and that group differences are largely heritable, and Nazi racism denied a shared human nature, so a common nature grounding equal dignity is rejected.

public-service-media.rationale: The Nazi state controlled media outright and white nationalists distrust mainstream media as hostile; funding independent public media is inferred to be rejected.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Racial nationalists include Christian, pagan and secular strands, and the sources do not tie the doctrine to any view of religious unity.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the Nazi 'blood and soil' valuing of the peasantry as racial stock and its state farm controls; modern strands say little, so this is low confidence.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on national strength and security of the racial state; the sources do not discuss nuclear arms.

workers-own-party.rationale: The movement organises around race, not class, so a separate workers' party competes with the racial party; inferred, as the sources do not address it.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred: white nationalists often cite such customs as proof of incompatibility with immigrant groups, though the sources do not discuss a ban.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the racial state's interest in the in-group's families and descent; the sources give no inheritance position and adherents may favour custom.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Language is peripheral to a race-based definition of the nation and adherents have no settled view on naming.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Economic and legal procedure is peripheral to the doctrine and adherents divide between statist and libertarian positions.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: the racial nation is defined by descent and a unitary state, leaving little place for a separate chiefly advisory body.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environmental questions are not discussed in the sources, and adherents divide between conservationist and anti-regulation positions.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the strong law-and-order emphasis of the movement; the sources do not address sentencing directly.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the stress on a shared national identity, though the movement's main aim is to restrict immigration rather than assimilate it.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Taylor and other adherents offer no common labour doctrine, and economic views vary widely, so the profile is neutral.

voter-id.rationale: Racial nationalists restrict membership of the nation by descent and press for tight control of who may vote and immigrate, so strict proof of citizenship is inferred as strongly supported.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Religious views vary widely across the strand and the sources do not address the question.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Adherents often distrust majoritarian democracy as a means of managing diversity and the Nazi form rejected it, so a purely procedural definition is inferred to be rejected.

premarital-sex.rationale: Racial nationalists mostly hold conservative views of sex and family and the Nazi racial state regulated sexuality, though modern adherents vary.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The Nazi form used censorship and emergency powers freely, and the movement's focus on order and security means shutdowns are inferred acceptable, though modern adherents complain of censorship.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Taylor opposes welfare that spreads resources across races, and adherents favour national solidarity over cash transfers; inferred as opposed.

women-suffrage.rationale: Modern adherents generally accept women's vote and office, while the Nazi form restricted women's public roles; the profile follows the mainstream modern strand.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Racial nationalists regard religion as one of the traditions of a people and not as the source of women's oppression; it is inferred, as the sources do not discuss it.

race-social-construct.rationale: Racial nationalism treats racial categories as real, largely innate biological groups, and Taylor and the Nazi race science claim a scientific basis for them.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Adherents hold that sex roles are natural and rank the nation's survival first; state gender-equality agencies are inferred as opposed.

missingStatements.text: Racial groups have distinct political interests, and members of each should organise to defend them.
missingStatements.rationale: Taylor argues that non-white groups already pursue explicitly racial interests and that whites should do the same, asking of such groups what is in it for them.

missingStatements.text: Pride in one's own race or ancestry is legitimate and should not be treated as shameful.
missingStatements.rationale: Taylor describes whites as discouraged from racial pride and calls for white racial consciousness, and he says apologies for past wrongs require neither honesty nor bravery.

notes: Black nationalism (Martin Delany, Garvey), Japanese and Korean racial nationalism and Nazi doctrine would answer many items differently, especially on supremacy, expansion, authoritarianism and religion. Modern Western adherents often disavow violence and Nazi methods, so the profile follows the mainstream modern strand where the strands diverge.
